raw_response:
My land here in Quzhou is flat North China Plain — the same land my father farmed. I've got about 15 mu. Every man I know in this village does wheat-corn rotation and I'm no different. It's what the market takes, what the grain depot buys, and what I know how to grow.

Wheat goes in the ground in October and comes off in June. Right after I clear the wheat straw I get the corn in fast — can't waste days when the season is short. That's how we double-crop and make the land work twice.

For wheat I'll plough before planting — my older tractor handles that. For corn I go straight in after wheat, no time for ploughing, I just do rotary or direct seed. Seeds I buy from the co-op — improved wheat variety, hybrid corn. No traditional seed anymore, yields are too low.

Fertilizer — I put down a base of compound fertilizer at planting and topdress nitrogen at jointing stage. Probably a bit more than the pamphlets say, but I'd rather not see yellow leaves. Water is the worry in Quzhou. The well is deeper every year. I'll irrigate wheat four times — pre-winter, jointing, heading, grain fill. Corn maybe twice unless it's a dry summer, then three.

Pesticide — spray wheat for rust and aphids, spray corn for borer. Two or three passes each crop.
